description: Verify the Hardware Address Length field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals ETHERNET_ADDR_LEN (6) — declares how many bytes each MAC address slot in the packet carries (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
ARP Request carries a hardware-address length byte that tells parsers how many bytes the sender_mac and target_mac fields occupy. For Ethernet MACs that is 6. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request and asserts the field value.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back; cache miss forces an ARP Request.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode        == 1
      - sender_mac    == DUT iface MAC
      - target_ip     == HOST-1-IP
      - hw_addr_len   == 6 (ETHERNET_ADDR_LEN)   ← key check

[Pass condition]
The observed ARP Request's Hardware Address Length equals 6.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_hw_addr_len — ARP Request seen but Hardware Address Length was not 6 (MAC field width mismatch)
• Fail_timeout — No ARP Request observed within the window

verdicts.Pass: ARP Request carried hw_addr_len=6 (Ethernet MAC width) — normal
verdicts.Fail_hw_addr_len: ARP Request emitted but hw_addr_len was not 6 — MAC field width mismatch
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP Request observed within the window
